settings.name_in_paper: Quantile MAB best-arm identification with 1-bit (threshold query) feedback, epsilon-relaxation
unmapped: Objective is the arm with highest q-quantile (not mean); identified arm must be within epsilon of the best q-quantile
Feedback is a single bit per pull: answer to learner-chosen threshold query 1{r <= gamma_t} (memoryless agent)
Rewards may be unbounded; only the q-quantile of each arm is assumed to lie in a known range [0, lambda]
The learner knows the quantile level q, the range lambda and the target accuracy epsilon
Algorithm need only be (epsilon,delta)-reliable: may fail to terminate on some instances
settings.definition_quote: The learner is given a set of arms $\A = \{1, 2, \dots, K\}$ with a stochastic reward setting... we assume the $q$-quantile of each arm to be bounded in a known range $[0, \lambda]$... We will focus on the threshold query model, where at iteration $t$, the side information $S_t$ is a query of the form ``Is $r_{a_t, t} \le \gamma_t$?'' and the 1-bit message is the corresponding binary feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Unquantized quantile MAB best-arm identification (lower bound)
unmapped: Objective is the arm with highest q-quantile within epsilon
q-quantiles lie in known range [0, lambda]; learner knows q, lambda and epsilon
settings.definition_quote: We present a worst-case lower bound on the expected number of arm pulls for the setup with no communication constraint.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-arm deterministic quantile bandit under threshold query model (lower bound)
unmapped: Feedback is the 1-bit answer to a threshold query 1{r <= gamma_t}
Rewards in known range [0, lambda]; learner knows q, lambda and epsilon
settings.definition_quote: Under the threshold query model, there exists a two-arm quantile bandit instance~$\nu$ with deterministic rewards

results.notes: Theorem stated under event E, which holds w.p. >= 1-delta (Lemma 2); Corollary 15 combines this with correctness: w.p. 1-delta returns an epsilon-optimal arm within this many pulls. Gaps are quantile-based, not mean gaps.

source.label: theorem: modified upper bound
source.quote: Under Event~$E$ as defined in Lemma~\ref{lem: good events}, the total number of arm pulls is upper bounded~by O(\sum_{k} \frac{1}{\max(\tilde\Delta_k,\tilde\Delta)^2}(\log(1/\delta)+\log(1/\max(\tilde\Delta_k,\tilde\Delta))+\log(c\lambda K/\epsilon)))

results.notes: Same algorithm, improved gaps (>= original). Holds under event E (prob >= 1-delta).

symbols.Delta_k: quantile arm gap of Definition 10 in the limit c -> infinity (independent of c and lambda)

conditions: exists a hard instance with unique best arm (worst-case over instances)

source.label: thm: lower bound unquantized
source.quote: Fix $q, \delta \in (0, 1)$ and $\lambda \ge 1$. There exists a quantile bandit instance~$\nu \in \cE$ with a unique best arm $k^*$ such that for any $\epsilon > 0$ satisfying ... and any $(\epsilon, \delta)$-reliable algorithm, the number of arm pulls $\tau$ satisfies $\E[\tau] \ge \Omega ( \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{1}{\Delta_k^2} \log ( \frac{1}{\delta} ) )$

results.notes: Holds without communication constraint (hence also with 1-bit feedback). Proof gives explicit constant: sum_j (1-q)^2/(27 Delta_j^2) log(1/(4 delta)). Instance adapted from Nikolakakis et al. Theorem 4.

source.label: thm: log lambda/epsilon dependence
source.quote: Fix $\lambda \ge \epsilon > 0$, and $q \in (0, 1)$, and $\delta \in (0, 0.5)$. Under the threshold query model, there exists a two-arm quantile bandit instance~$\nu$ with deterministic rewards such that any $(\epsilon, \delta)$-reliable algorithm requires $\Omega(\log(\lambda/ \epsilon))$ arm pulls.

results.notes: Probability type not explicit; the argument is a worst-case information-counting bound on the number of queries. Recorded as expectation with uncertainty.
